segments: This tutorial retains examples using the NixOS/Home Manager 24.05 branches to illustrate structure, not to recommend deploying this historical release. Real configurations should use compatible, supported branches, retain the existing stateVersion, and check interfaces against the locked versions. Placeholder commits/hashes and ellipses must be replaced. The code has not been built or run on the target system.
This chapter covers Nix's most important advance. Flakes provide reproducible, version-locked project definitions.
Flakes are an experimental Nix feature that provides:
Reproducibility: all dependencies are locked through flake.lock
Or enable them temporarily with command-line flags:
How Do I Inspect the Outputs a Flake Provides?
How Do I Debug a Build Failure?
How Do I Reference a Local Path?
How Do I Support Legacy Entry Points?

nix-build does not automatically convert a flake into a traditional expression. The project needs to provide default.nix/shell.nix; flake-compat can adapt the locked flake. Only after adding that adapter should you use:
Separate system configurations: a dedicated directory for each host
Back up the lock file: keep it in version control
